## P6-Q1 — зоны vs пакеты

**Query:** Answer in prose, no tables. Modular monolith internal modules versus
splitting a kernel into many Composer packages: when are namespace directories
plus architecture tests enough, and when does a separate package become
justified? Cite Fowler modular monolith, Symfony bundles versus components,
Drupal modules, Shopware. What costs does a one-file Composer package add
(version, CI, split repo, BC surface)? Name primary-source URLs.

**Status:** success

For a product deployed as one system under one team, keep capabilities as
internal modules first: namespace directories, explicit contracts, and
architecture tests. Extract a Composer package only when you need an
independently released, independently consumed, or independently governed
artifact.

Martin Fowler’s modular-monolith / Monolith First argument is about strong
module boundaries in a single deployable. Symfony’s current guidance: do not
use bundles to organize application code; bundles are for sharing features
across applications. Components are independently reusable libraries. Drupal
modules and Shopware plugins/apps are extension units with install/uninstall
lifecycle — justified when that lifecycle is real, excessive for an internal
Orders slice of one product.

Directories plus CI are enough when the capability has the same release
cadence, the same owners, and the need is preventing accidental coupling, not
distribution. A Composer package is justified by multiple real consumers,
independent release, independent ownership, a stable narrow API, or a heavy
optional dependency the host should be able to omit.

A one-file package adds versioning obligation, a public BC surface, release
coordination across repos, duplicated CI, and supply-chain overhead without
autonomy if everyone still deploys together.

Primary sources: https://martinfowler.com/bliki/MonolithFirst.html ·
https://symfony.com/doc/current/bundles.html ·
https://simonbrown.je/modular-monolith/ ·
https://getcomposer.org/doc/02-libraries.md ·
https://www.drupal.org/docs/user_guide/en/understanding-modules.html

## P6-Q2 — class_alias и SemVer при переносе FQCN

**Query:** Answer in prose, no tables. PHP PSR-4 namespace moves of public
classes: is class_alias from the new FQCN to the old FQCN a SemVer-compatible
deprecation, or still a break? How should stub files versus a Composer autoload
files aliases.php be written so PHPStan and Roave BackwardCompatibilityCheck
treat the old name as existing? Cite PHP class_alias docs, Composer autoload
files, Roave/BackwardCompatibilityCheck, Symfony deprecation policy. Name
primary-source URLs.

**Status:** success

`class_alias(New::class, Old::class)` preserves runtime identity: PHP documents
the alias as exactly the same class. It is SemVer-compatible only if the old
FQCN remains autoloadable for the whole minor line. Symfony BC promise: changing
a class name or namespace is not a compatible change; keep the old API through
deprecation.

Composer `autoload.files` is included whenever `vendor/autoload.php` is loaded —
suitable for runtime aliases, not for a source-level declaration.

PHPStan and Roave inspect declared symbols. A deleted PSR-4 file plus an
imperative alias can be reported as removal. The robust library pattern is a
real old-FQCN forwarding subclass. That pattern is unavailable for `final`
classes (cannot extend). For `final`, either keep the old file or accept that
Roave sees a structural removal and pin an explained exception.

Do not combine a same-name wrapper and `class_alias` for one FQCN.

Primary sources: https://www.php.net/manual/en/function.class-alias.php ·
https://getcomposer.org/doc/04-schema.md ·
https://github.com/Roave/BackwardCompatibilityCheck ·
https://symfony.com/doc/current/contributing/code/bc.html ·
https://symfony.com/doc/current/contributing/code/conventions.html#deprecations

## P6-Q3 — autoload-dev и Testbench в production PSR-4

**Query:** Answer in prose, no tables. Composer autoload versus autoload-dev:
when package A is required by package B as a production path repository, does B
receive A's autoload-dev? Why is shipping an Orchestra Testbench TestCase
subclass in a Laravel package production PSR-4 autoload a problem if Testbench
is only require-dev? What is the accepted placement for a reusable package
TestCase? Cite Composer docs autoload-dev, orchestra/testbench, Laravel package
development docs. Name primary-source URLs.

**Status:** success

No. `autoload-dev` and `require-dev` are root-only. A path repository changes
where Composer obtains the package; it does not make it another root. Consumers
of A receive A's production `autoload` only.

Shipping `Tests\TestCase extends Orchestra\Testbench\TestCase` through
production PSR-4 advertises a class whose parent is not in the runtime
dependency graph. Reflection, optimized autoload, or accidental reference can
fail even if the app never runs the package tests.

Accepted placement: `tests/TestCase.php` under `autoload-dev`, Testbench in
`require-dev`. If a class is intentionally a supported downstream test API, it
must not extend a require-dev type — either promote the dependency to
`require` (usually wrong) or keep a Testbench-free abstraction and let each
consumer own its adapter.

Primary sources: https://getcomposer.org/doc/04-schema.md ·
https://packages.tools/testbench ·
https://laravel.com/docs/13.x/packages
